title: Determine and interrupt the disease process associated with chronic traumatic encephalopathy

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a connected capability: identify the pathology associated with chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) during life, determine which biological processes connect repetitive head impacts to pathology and clinical impairment, and safely interrupt the processes responsible for harm. Its aim is to turn an uncertain relationship among exposure, disease and symptoms into a basis for reliable prevention and treatment. This is a research objective, not an achieved diagnostic or therapeutic capability.

The concept requires distinguishing three things: a history of repetitive head impacts, a clinical syndrome involving symptoms or functional impairment, and the presence of a particular underlying pathology. Establishing one does not, by itself, establish the others or explain their causal relationship. The supplied research identifies nonspecific symptoms, variation in exposure and outcomes, and reliance on postmortem examination as motivating difficulties. Those assertions remain part of the research rationale, but the supplied review could not verify them from the retained scientific source.

significance.text: Conditional significance: reliable identification during life, combined with causal understanding and an effective intervention, could create a major neurological prevention and treatment capability. It could make it possible to identify people likely to benefit, select treatment according to the harmful process actually operating, and evaluate whether intervention changes clinically meaningful outcomes. Establishing reproducible risk relationships could also improve the evidential basis for prevention decisions concerning repetitive head impacts.

The potential impact depends on what an intervention accomplishes. Preventing future injury, slowing an established disease process, stopping further decline and restoring lost abilities are separate achievements. A change in a pathology-linked measure—including a hypothetical reduction in tau pathology—would not alone demonstrate recovered cognition or everyday function. Even a successful disease-modifying intervention would need separate evidence before claims of functional restoration were justified. The supplied material does not establish that tau clearance is an effective treatment or that it reverses impairment.

Conditional downstream possibility: methods developed here might inform other injury-related or neurodegenerative conditions if shared mechanisms were demonstrated. That possibility does not imply that CTE, Alzheimer’s disease and other disorders have interchangeable causes, diagnostic measures or treatments. The broader significance would depend on evidence of transferable mechanisms and clinical benefit in each relevant population.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in this proposal is to connect a trustworthy measure of relevant pathology during life with a causal account of impairment and an intervention that improves outcomes. A diagnostic development program would need to determine whether candidate measures identify the intended pathology, distinguish it from other explanations for symptoms, and remain informative across different exposure histories and stages of illness. These are requirements of the proposed capability; the supplied evidence does not establish the present performance or availability of any particular test.

The causal barrier is more demanding than finding an association between head impacts, a biological marker and later symptoms. Reproducible prospective associations could establish risk relationships, but confounding and alternative explanations would still need to be addressed. Complementary designs must distinguish the effects of exposure, pathology and other contributors to impairment, and determine which processes are causal targets rather than accompanying signs of disease.

The intervention barrier is to alter a harmful process safely and produce meaningful clinical benefit. Researchers would need to establish when intervention can help, whether benefit persists, and whether biological changes correspond to preserved or improved function. Restoring established losses adds a further challenge: stopping ongoing damage does not by itself demonstrate recovery of abilities already lost.

current_state.text: The supplied review verified the identity of a 2021 article by Katz and colleagues, National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for Traumatic Encephalopathy Syndrome, DOI 10.1212/WNL.0000000000011850. Its bibliographic content establishes that it concerns consensus diagnostic criteria for traumatic encephalopathy syndrome. However, the retained copy ends within the author affiliations, before the abstract and scientific body, so the review had no inspectable scientific passages supporting the substantive diagnostic or treatment claims.

The earlier research described those criteria as intended for research and distinguished traumatic encephalopathy syndrome from definitive identification of CTE pathology. It also described validated diagnosis during life and reversal of established CTE as remaining gaps. Those statements cannot be confirmed from the supplied excerpt because the cited abstract and introduction are absent. The distinction between a clinical syndrome and underlying pathology remains essential to defining this innovation, but this record cannot attribute a verified account of that distinction to the unseen portions of the article.

The supplied material does not establish the state of diagnostic validation or treatment efficacy as of the review’s reference date, November 1, 2026. No freshness assessment was supplied, and retrieval of a 2021 article on November 11, 2026 does not update its scientific conclusions. No inspectable results here establish diagnostic accuracy, causal effect sizes, treatment benefit or durable reversal. This limitation leaves those questions open; it is not evidence that the earlier assertions are false or that relevant achievements do not exist.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: independently validate measures intended to identify relevant pathology during life, with an explicit account of the reference evidence used to establish what they detect. Prospective studies should then show reproducible relationships among exposure, measured pathology and subsequent clinical outcomes. Validation should report errors, uncertainty and performance across the populations and disease stages actually studied. These are proposed requirements, not an established completion standard.
completion_criteria.label: Independently validated in-life pathology measures reproducibly predict subsequent clinical outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal demonstration: combine prospective observation with complementary designs capable of distinguishing causation from confounding. The evidence should support specific pathways connecting exposure, pathology and impairment, test plausible alternative explanations, and identify which steps can be altered to change outcomes. Repetition of an association alone would not meet this causal requirement.
completion_criteria.label: Causal, modifiable pathways connect exposure, pathology and clinical impairment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed therapeutic demonstration: controlled trials should show that an intervention safely prevents clinically meaningful decline or improves established impairment in a clearly defined population. Biological measures can support interpretation, but the claim should be anchored in clinical outcomes and everyday function. A claim of reversal would require durable functional improvement beyond a change in a pathology-linked marker.
completion_criteria.label: Interventions safely prevent meaningful decline or improve established impairment

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent studies should reproduce the diagnostic and therapeutic findings and specify exposure histories, clinical characteristics, timing, follow-up duration and safety limits. Claims should remain within those demonstrated conditions. Success in finite studies would establish breadth across the tested settings, not universal diagnosis, prevention or reversal for every person with repetitive head-impact exposure.
completion_criteria.label: Independent studies reproduce diagnostic and therapeutic findings within stated limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: NRL-09, Prevent Alzheimer’s dementia before irreversible functional loss, overlaps with the prevention objective; NRL-11, Halt established Alzheimer’s disease and restore lost function, overlaps with the distinction between stopping progression and restoring abilities. NRL-18 retains its focus on the disease process associated with CTE. The supplied material does not establish that diagnostic measures or therapies would transfer among these conditions.

Roster-based synthesis: NRL-15, Identify and treat shared mechanisms of neurodegeneration across diseases, could connect to NRL-18 if causal mechanisms shared with other disorders were demonstrated. NRL-15 seeks generality across diseases, whereas NRL-18 requires a defensible account of the particular relationships among repetitive head impacts, CTE-associated pathology and impairment. Neither objective substitutes for the other.

Roster-based synthesis: NRL-04, Read and selectively repair the physical traces of specific memories, and NRL-06, Replace lost brain tissue while preserving learned function, concern forms of repair that might become relevant to restoring established losses. NRL-18 could achieve meaningful prevention or disease interruption without either capability; conversely, a repair capability would not itself establish what causes CTE-associated impairment. NRL-10, Safe, programmable delivery to selected cells throughout the human brain, could enable a future targeted intervention if such delivery were required, but delivery alone would establish neither a causal target nor clinical benefit.

change_log.change: Preserved NRL-18’s identity and integrated identification during life, causal explanation and safe intervention into one coherent objective.
change_log.reason: These are complementary parts of the supplied concept, and limited supporting evidence does not justify deleting the innovation.

change_log.change: Qualified the earlier claims about symptom specificity, exposure variability, postmortem diagnosis, research criteria and remaining treatment gaps.
change_log.reason: The review verified the article’s identity but found that the retained copy ended before the scientific content needed to substantiate those claims.

change_log.change: Separated verified bibliographic information from unverified scientific claims and unassessed present-day status.
change_log.reason: A 2026 retrieval date does not establish scientific currency, and no freshness assessment was supplied.

change_log.change: Strengthened the proposed causal demonstration to require designs that distinguish causation from confounding.
change_log.reason: Prospective measurement and reproducible associations alone do not establish causal pathways.

change_log.change: Preserved the distinction among prevention, slowing progression, stopping decline and restoring lost function.
change_log.reason: Biological change or tau clearance alone would not demonstrate durable functional recovery.

change_log.change: Expanded proposed validation, replication and practical boundaries, and explained relevant roster overlaps without merging entries.
change_log.reason: A convincing achievement needs interpretable scope and clinical benefit; related prevention, repair and delivery capabilities remain distinct objectives.

unresolved_issues: The supplied scientific source is truncated before its abstract and body. Its substantive account of traumatic encephalopathy syndrome criteria and their relationship to CTE pathology remains unverified here.
The supplied evidence does not resolve the earlier assertions about symptom specificity, variability in exposure and outcomes, or reliance on postmortem diagnosis.
No freshness assessment establishes which diagnostic and therapeutic gaps remained open as of November 1, 2026.
The material does not identify validated pathology-linked measures, their reference standards or diagnostic performance.
Causal pathways, intervention targets, clinical efficacy, safety and durable restoration of established impairment remain undetermined by the supplied evidence.
The completion criteria are proposals; numerical thresholds, follow-up duration and acceptable practical limits would require further justification.

brief.title: Finding and stopping brain disease linked to head blows
possible: People exposed to repeated head blows could learn whether they have chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a disease involving harmful brain changes. Doctors could identify what drives the harm and offer treatments that safely slow decline or improve lost abilities.
why: This could help doctors choose treatments for the harmful process affecting each person and measure whether treatment preserves thinking and everyday abilities. Clearer links between head impacts and disease could also guide prevention decisions.

sources.showed: The work sets out agreed diagnostic criteria for traumatic encephalopathy syndrome, a pattern of symptoms associated with CTE.
sources.cited_for: It provides a framework for studying symptoms associated with CTE.
sources.not_established: Symptom criteria alone do not establish the underlying brain changes or an effective treatment.

sources.showed: A study of six former American football players compared brain scans with CTE-related changes found after death. Scan readings overlapped between people with and without CTE.
sources.cited_for: It tests whether scans during life correspond to disease found after death.
sources.not_established: The small study does not establish a reliable test that distinguishes CTE from its absence.

sources.showed: Head-impact exposure was associated with CTE outcomes in male football players. Similar relationships remained among players without military or other contact-sport exposure.
sources.cited_for: It supports a relationship between repeated head impacts and CTE.
sources.not_established: An association does not identify the biological steps that cause impairment or prove that changing them helps.

sources.showed: Among 364 brain donors with CTE, greater buildup of altered tau (p-tau), a characteristic brain change, was associated with worse reported thinking and daily function.
sources.quote:
Accumulation of p‑tau aggregates, especially in the frontal cortex, are associated with cognitive, func‑
tional, and certain neurobehavioral symptoms in CTE.
sources.cited_for: It links the amount and location of disease-related brain changes to symptoms.
sources.not_established: The study does not prove that removing tau would prevent decline or restore abilities.

shown: Researchers have connected parts of the picture: head-impact exposure, brain changes and reported impairment. The progress remains observational; it does not yet connect reliable diagnosis during life to a treatment that improves everyday function.
missing: A reliable test during life must distinguish CTE-related brain changes from other explanations for symptoms.
Researchers must identify which biological processes cause harm and can be changed to improve outcomes.
Controlled trials must demonstrate safe, lasting benefits in thinking and everyday function.

milestones.label: Independent tests during life predict later outcomes
milestones.explanation: Independently validated tests would have to identify CTE-related brain changes and reproducibly predict later health outcomes alongside exposure history. This would connect detection to what happens to people.

milestones.label: Changeable biological processes explain how head impacts cause impairment
milestones.explanation: Complementary studies would have to distinguish cause from coincidence and identify changeable steps linking impacts, brain changes and impairment. This would establish targets for treatment.

milestones.label: Treatment safely prevents decline or improves established impairment
milestones.explanation: Controlled trials would have to show safe prevention of meaningful decline or improvement in established impairment. Lasting gains in everyday function would be needed to claim reversal.

milestones.label: Independent studies reproduce diagnosis and treatment results
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to reproduce diagnostic and treatment findings across clearly described groups, treatment timings and safety limits. This would establish where the benefits hold.

uncertain: It remains unclear when interrupting the disease process could help, and whether lost abilities could recover.
The accuracy required of tests, the duration of follow-up and acceptable safety limits still need justification.

page.title: Diagnosis and disease modification of chronic traumatic encephalopathy
page.definition: A test identifies chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) during life, and a treatment slows the disease enough to preserve cognition or everyday function. Neuropathologists confirm CTE after death by finding abnormal tau protein in neurons around small blood vessels at the depths of grooves in the brain’s surface. Traumatic encephalopathy syndrome (TES) describes clinical features after repeated head impacts. Those features alone do not establish CTE.

goal.need: At least 24.5% of former National Football League players who died in 2016–21 had CTE at death. In a separate brain bank, only six of 25 donors who met clinical criteria for TES had CTE at autopsy. A reliable diagnosis could help patients enter appropriate treatment trials while clinicians assess other treatable causes of their symptoms. Current care can ease depression or anxiety. Slowing CTE itself could help people retain memory and independence in daily life.

figures.caption: Performance of the 2014 TES criteria against autopsy findings.
figures.note: Retrospective assessment of 298 brain donors: 224 with CTE and 74 without. These estimates do not describe the revised 2021 criteria.

statements.body: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke
statements.quote: A primary recommendation from this workshop was the need to develop diagnostics for CTE in living persons.
statements.context: Funding announcement RFA-NS-19-026 summarises the institute's 2012 CTE neuropathology workshop.

statements.body: 2025 Leon Thal Summit expert panel, hosted by Cleveland Clinic Lou Ruvo Center for Brain Health
statements.quote: therapies to arrest, slow, or prevent the progression of CTE are needed.

completion.title: A controlled human trial demonstrates clinically beneficial modification of CTE.
completion.criterion: A prospectively registered, randomised controlled human trial in participants identified during life by a CTE assay validated against postmortem neuropathology demonstrates slower cognitive or functional decline, together with evidence that treatment alters the implicated CTE disease process. Its prespecified efficacy and safety criteria are met. Diagnostic cutoffs, minimum benefit and follow-up must be justified in that protocol; no universal numerical thresholds were located.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; provisional combined test because no outside body was found to define the complete diagnostic-and-treatment achievement.
completion.basis: Searched NINDS CTE/TES consensus documents, NIH CTE funding calls and the 2025 Leon Thal Summit recommendations for a joint diagnostic-and-treatment test; none defined one or supplied numerical accuracy, benefit or follow-up thresholds. This provisional Atlas test combines pathology-validated diagnosis with the Summit's goal of altering progression.

milestones.title: Postmortem brain tissue contains at least one CTE-defining cortical lesion.
milestones.criterion: Find at least one cortical lesion with phosphorylated tau aggregates in neurons around a small blood vessel at the depth of a cortical groove. The lesion must involve deeper cortical layers. Tau in astrocytes may accompany the neuronal deposits, but astrocytic tau alone is insufficient.
milestones.set_by: Second NINDS/NIBIB neuropathology consensus panel; diagnostic criteria published in 2021.
milestones.threshold_quote: The group endorsed a single pathognomonic lesion in the cortex as the minimum threshold for CTE.

milestones.title: An assay validated against brain pathology distinguishes CTE from other tau diseases during life.
milestones.criterion: Measure the candidate marker by imaging or in a body fluid during life. Compare the results with postmortem neuropathological diagnoses in the same individuals, including people with other diseases involving abnormal tau, and show that the assay distinguishes CTE from those diseases.
milestones.set_by: 2025 Leon Thal Summit expert panel, Recommendation 1, published on May 12, 2026.
milestones.threshold_quote: Clinicopathologically validated assays capable of distinguishing CTE from other tauopathies are required

milestones.title: An investigational new drug application takes effect for a US clinical study of a CTE treatment.
milestones.criterion: Pharmacology and toxicology data support the sponsor’s conclusion that the proposed investigation is reasonably safe, and the investigational new drug application is in effect. It takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless FDA imposes a clinical hold, or earlier if FDA notifies the sponsor that the investigation may begin.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.23(a)(8) and 312.40; general investigational-drug requirements applied to a CTE candidate.
milestones.threshold_quote: it is reasonably safe to conduct the proposed clinical investigations.

milestones.title: Human dosing yields enough pharmacology and safety information to design Phase 2 testing of a CTE drug.
milestones.criterion: Initial human studies characterise drug disposition, pharmacological actions and side effects with increasing doses sufficiently to design scientifically valid, controlled Phase 2 studies. Participants may be healthy volunteers or appropriate patients. FDA specifies no universal sample size, tolerated adverse-event rate or exposure duration for this transition.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase I Clinical Studies; a general development criterion applied to a CTE candidate.
milestones.threshold_quote: permit the design of well-controlled, scientifically valid, Phase 2 studies.

milestones.title: Controlled Phase 2 testing yields preliminary evidence that a CTE-directed drug is effective.
milestones.criterion: Controlled studies in the intended patient population obtain preliminary evidence of effectiveness for the proposed indication and characterise common short-term side effects and risks, supporting subsequent Phase 3 evaluation. FDA's published phase definitions supply this transition criterion without prescribing a CTE-specific endpoint, minimum effect size or follow-up duration.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Drug Development and Review Definitions, Phase 2 and Phase 3 Clinical Studies; general criteria applied to CTE drug development.
milestones.threshold_quote: preliminary evidence suggesting effectiveness of the drug has been obtained in Phase 2

milestones.title: A study measures neurodegenerative change over 3–5 years in symptomatic people at high risk for CTE.
milestones.criterion: Follow symptomatic participants at high risk for CTE and appropriate controls for 3–5 years. Use repeated clinical assessments and biological measures, such as brain imaging or blood or cerebrospinal fluid markers, to characterize the course of neurodegeneration. The interval applies to this natural-history study.
milestones.set_by: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, RFA-NS-14-012, 2014.
milestones.threshold_quote: progression of the neurodegeneration over a 3 - 5 year period in symptomatic individuals considered to be at high risk for CTE.

not_found: No CTE-specific numerical standard for diagnostic accuracy, minimum clinical benefit or follow-up was located in the searched consensus documents and funding calls.
No primary report of a controlled human trial demonstrating clinically beneficial modification of CTE was located.
No public FDA clearance letter for IND 32912 or report of actual enrollment, dosing or patient outcomes in NCT07958925 was located.

results.finding: In 298 UNITE brain donors, the 2014 clinical TES criteria had 20.27% specificity for autopsy-confirmed CTE.
results.detail: These performance estimates apply to the 2014 TES criteria. The paper reports the newer NINDS criteria as a consensus outcome.
results.quote: The 2014 criteria were evaluated with respect to sensitivity and specificity in predicting a pathologic diagnosis of CTE in the UNITE study (CTE, n = 224; no CTE, n = 74). Sensitivity was high (97.32); specificity was low (20.27).

results.finding: Of six former American football players examined at autopsy, four had a CTE-defining cortical lesion.
results.quote: The remaining four cases had CTE (cases 3–6).

results.finding: In six former American football players, cortical flortaucipir PET uptake correlated with postmortem phosphorylated tau density (Spearman ρ = 0.71).
results.detail: The CTE cases were all high stage. Known off-target binding in the hippocampus and thalamus further limited interpretation.

results.finding: Postmortem examination found CTE-defining pathology in 451 of 631 male American tackle football brain donors.
results.detail: Four neuropathologists reviewed the diagnoses. The article reports donor-level diagnoses and stages. Individual lesion counts and layer-by-layer findings are unspecified.
results.quote: 180 athletes did not have CTE, 163 had low-stage CTE (Stage I or II), and 288 had high-stage CTE (Stage III or IV).

results.finding: In 1 illustrated donor from a 364-donor autopsy cohort, perivascular neuronal tau at sulcal depths was documented in 4 cortical regions.
results.detail: The caption identifies layer 4 for entorhinal tangles and neurites but does not describe those deposits as a perivascular lesion at a sulcal depth.
results.quote:
Photomicrographs of AT8 immunostained cortical neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), 
neurites, and astrocytic inclusions around small central vessels within the depths of sulci in a 71‑ year‑old former professional American 
football player with stage IV CTE

results.finding: PET in 3 athletes with suspected CTE and 7 healthy controls showed elevated ¹⁸F-OXD-2314 uptake at the gray–white matter junction and in white matter.
results.detail: The reported PET comparison used healthy controls. The release mentions other non-Alzheimer’s tauopathies without giving comparative results.
results.quote:

results.finding: In 49 healthy volunteers dosed with PNT001 or placebo, cerebrospinal fluid exposure exceeded the antibody’s binding constant at doses of 900 mg or higher.
results.detail: The authors concluded that the single-dose findings supported multiple-dose patient studies in tauopathies.
results.quote: These data indicate that single doses of PNT001 of 900 mg and above can achieve a sustained CSF concentration above the antigen-antibody Kd.

results.finding: Among 16 brain donors, 7 had neuropathologically confirmed CTE.
results.detail: The paper reports consensus verification without describing individual lesions.
results.quote: We first verified that participants with neuropathological diagnoses of CTE based on prior criteria also met recent consensus criteria (e.g., required neuronal tau inclusions)

results.finding: Among 16 autopsied donors, 4 plasma protein modules were significantly elevated in donors with CTE.
results.detail: All CTE-positive donors had mixed neuropathology. The reported classifier evaluated repetitive head impact exposure, and the autopsy comparison provided no CTE classification performance.
results.quote: Plasma proteomic signatures in our living RHI cohort were recapitulated in a subset of seven brain donors with autopsy-confirmed CTE, where M1, M2, M4, and M9 were all significantly elevated compared to nine brain donors without CTE.

results.finding: One patient described as having CTE received expanded-access ABBV-8E12 infusions at doses up to 25 mg/kg.
results.detail: The sponsor protocol documents the doses administered to the CTE patient. Its measured pharmacokinetic and safety findings come from a separate PSP study.
results.quote:
The CTE patient has received multiple infusions 
of ABBV-8E12 from 2.5 to 25 mg/kg.
